# Mathilde Pedersen

Mathilde Pedersen is a quality consultant and data steward representative serving on the steering group of [[danibd|DANIBD]], Denmark's national database for inflammatory bowel disease. In this role, she represents the data-responsible authority from SundK, the Danish Health Data Authority.[^src1]

Pedersen's involvement with DANIBD situates her within the governance structure of a major national health registry. [[danibd|DANIBD]] encompasses patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) treated across Denmark's public hospital system, including those with Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, short bowel syndrome, and primary sclerosing cholangitis. The database maintains a coverage rate estimated to exceed 90 percent, validated against regional registries.[^src1] As a steering group member, Pedersen participates in oversight of a registry that aggregates data from six national health registers and includes patients with at least two hospital contacts for specified IBD conditions. The steering group itself represents all five Danish regions, patient representatives, and data administrators—making Pedersen's role as a data steward from SundK a key institutional bridge between the registry and Denmark's health data governance framework.[^src1]
